stories.summary: Republicans and Democrats object over Trump’s role in Jensen Huang’s return as Nvidia CEO, following an affair with an alleged Chinese spy Republican senators criticize Nvidia’s decision to reinstate Jensen Huang Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia, despite concerns over his conduct and the supply of AI chips to China, may show that AI – and Huang himself – are ‘too big to fail’. That phrase was on everyone’s lips almost 20 years ago when the Global Financial Crisis struck, and several major banks were bailed out. Given Nvidia’s pivotal role in the AI capex rollout, the implications of Huang’s reinstatement could be profound. Borrowing from the GFC, are some technology CEOs now so systemically important to the future of AI and US leadership in the latest technology revolution that they cannot be fired? Questions around the scale of financing required and future monetisation remain, and the dependence on Huang for the future success of AI may paradoxically heighten those concerns especially given Anthropic fell despite yesterday’s broad market rally. “We must investigate these actions. stories.title: Timms says Pip review being published today will ‘rehumanise’ benefit – UK politics live
stories.summary: Some recommendations expected to clash with those of Milburn’s recent report into Neets UK disability benefit cuts ‘risk worsening youth destitution’ Libby Brooks has a good explainer about Pip in her First Edition newsletter today. She sets out how Pip was created by the coalition government in response to a “culture war” over benefits, and she describes how the Timms review and the Alan Miliburn review have been at odds. Here is an extract. Last week’s Milburn review called for Pip to be scrapped for younger claimants, and for the health element of universal credit to be replaced by an additional cost allowance, part of a wider network of job-based help for this age group. The shock among the organisations which had contributed to Timms was palpable, says Patrick [Butler , the Guardian’s social affairs editor]. “The idea that you basically blow up Pip for younger people took a lot of groups by surprise.” Sporting organisations will be required to demonstrate “structural equality” to receive public funding as part of the drive, the government said.
